executive_summary.summary: The platform's primary path (Mobile App -> API Gateway -> Account API -> Account Database) is reasonably controlled, but a legacy offline-sync path lets the mobile app write directly to the Account Database with no documented authentication, authorization, or encryption, bypassing the API Gateway entirely. Object-level authorization on the Account API and the security posture of the Admin Portal are also undocumented.
top_risks: Legacy mobile-to-database sync path bypasses the API Gateway and has no documented authentication, authorization, or encryption.
Account API authorization model is undocumented; object-level authorization (BOLA) cannot be confirmed.
Notification Service (third party) receives customer PII via a call with undocumented authentication.
key_recommendations: Retire the legacy mobile-to-database sync path, or route it through the API Gateway with the same authentication/authorization controls as the primary path.
Confirm and, if missing, implement server-side object-level authorization in the Account API.
Document and restrict Admin Portal network exposure to an admin-only network segment.
major_unknowns: Authentication used for the Account API -> Notification Service webhook call.

included: Mobile Banking Platform: Mobile App, API Gateway, Account API, Account Database, Notification Service, Admin Portal
assumptions: The API Gateway terminates TLS and forwards over HTTPS internally.
Admin Portal network exposure is not documented and is treated as unconfirmed.

data_flows: Mobile App -> API Gateway (CALLS, HTTPS, OAuth2)
Mobile App -> Account Database (WRITES_TO, legacy offline sync)
Account API -> Notification Service (SENDS_DATA_TO, HTTPS webhook)

open_questions.question: Does the Account API enforce object-level authorization on every account lookup, or does it rely solely on the API Gateway's OAuth2 token?
open_questions.reason: Account API handles customer-owned financial data and sits behind a single OAuth2 check at the gateway.

open_questions.question: Is the Admin Portal restricted to a dedicated admin network segment, or reachable from the general corporate network?
open_questions.reason: Admin Portal administers the Account Database and its network exposure is undocumented.

open_questions.question: What authentication (if any) protects the legacy mobile-to-database offline sync path?
open_questions.reason: This path writes directly to the database bypassing the API Gateway and Account API entirely.

questionnaire_results.question: Is object-level authorization enforced server-side for every operation that accesses a user-owned or tenant-owned resource?
questionnaire_results.reason: No evidence of object-level authorization enforcement was found in the reviewed architecture document.

questionnaire_results.reason: No authorization model was documented for either component.

threats.title: Undocumented object-level authorization in Account API
threats.attack_scenario: An authenticated mobile user manipulates an account identifier to view or modify another customer's balance or transaction history, if the Account API relies only on the API Gateway's authentication and does not independently verify resource ownership.
preconditions: Object-level authorization is undocumented at the Account API layer
threats.impact: Unauthorized access to another customer's financial data.
evidence: Known Gaps section of architecture.md flags this as an open TODO
assumptions: API Gateway performs authentication only, not object-level authorization

threats.title: Legacy mobile-to-database sync path bypasses API layer
threats.attack_scenario: The mobile app writes directly to the Account Database for offline sync, bypassing the API Gateway and Account API. If the mobile client embeds direct database credentials or an unauthenticated path, any compromise of the app or its traffic grants direct write access to account data.
preconditions: Mobile app has network-reachable direct access to the Account Database
No confirmed authentication, authorization, or encryption on this path
threats.impact: Unauthorized read/write access to customer financial data, potentially bypassing all API-layer controls.
evidence: Overview and Known Gaps sections of architecture.md; Mermaid diagram shows a direct Mobile App -> Account Database edge

threats.title: Customer PII sent to third-party Notification Service without confirmed authentication
threats.attack_scenario: The Account API calls the Notification Service webhook with customer name, phone number, and transaction amount. Without confirmed request authentication, a spoofed or intercepted call path could disclose or inject notification data.
preconditions: Call crosses a trust boundary to an external third party
threats.impact: Disclosure of customer PII to an unauthenticated party, or injected fraudulent notifications.

attack_paths.title: External attacker abuses the legacy sync path to reach account data directly
required_weaknesses: Legacy sync path has no confirmed authentication or authorization
Path bypasses API Gateway and Account API controls entirely
attack_paths.impact: Direct unauthorized read/write access to customer account data.
recommended_controls: Retire the legacy sync path or route it through the API Gateway
Require the same authentication/authorization on this path as the primary API path

preventive: Enforce server-side object-level authorization on every Account API operation that accepts an account or customer identifier.
Use centralized authorization middleware rather than per-endpoint checks.
detective: Log and alert on denied authorization attempts and identifier-enumeration patterns.
corrective: Revoke affected sessions and audit access logs if unauthorized access is confirmed.
compensating: Add API Gateway-level checks restricting callers to their own account identifiers while the Account API fix is implemented.

preventive: Retire the legacy mobile-to-database sync path.
If it must remain, route it through the API Gateway and Account API with the same authentication, authorization, and TLS requirements as the primary path.
detective: Alert on any direct network connection from mobile IP ranges to the Account Database.
corrective: Rotate any credentials used by the legacy sync path immediately if it is found to be unauthenticated.
compensating: Restrict Account Database network access to only the Account API's service identity as an interim control.

preventive: Authenticate the Account API -> Notification Service webhook call (e.g., signed requests or mutual TLS).
detective: Monitor and alert on webhook call failures or unexpected volume.
compensating: Minimize the customer data fields sent to the Notification Service to only what is strictly required.

recommendations.reason: No preset reaches the 60.0% coverage threshold for the requested CWEs in Java (best was 'All' at 50.0%): CWE-306 (missing authentication) has zero matching Java queries in the Checkmarx catalog, so no preset can cover it.

sast_recommendations.scan_recommendation: Scan Account API controller/handler methods that accept an account or customer identifier for missing ownership/authorization checks before data access.

sast_recommendations.focus_area: Hardcoded credentials / direct database access from a client
sast_recommendations.scan_recommendation: Scan the mobile app codebase for embedded database connection strings, credentials, or direct DB client libraries.
Review the Notification Service webhook client code for signed-request or mutual-TLS authentication and for the specific fields transmitted.

dast_recommendations.test_objective: Verify that an authenticated user cannot access another user's account or transaction data by modifying object identifiers.
high_level_steps: Authenticate as Test User A and capture valid account resource requests.
Authenticate as Test User B and attempt to access User A's resources by changing identifiers.
Attempt safe enumeration of account identifiers within approved test data.
dast_recommendations.expected_secure_behavior: The API denies cross-account access without revealing whether the target identifier exists.
dast_recommendations.safety_note: Run only against an authorized test environment or approved production-safe test accounts.

dast_recommendations.test_objective: Confirm the legacy mobile-to-database sync path requires authentication and rejects unauthenticated or replayed requests.
high_level_steps: Identify the network path/protocol used by the legacy sync feature in a test environment.
Attempt a sync request without valid credentials/session.
Attempt a sync request replaying a captured request from a different test account.
dast_recommendations.expected_secure_behavior: Unauthenticated or replayed sync requests are rejected.
dast_recommendations.safety_note: Test only in an authorized non-production environment with test accounts and test data.

dast_recommendations.test_name: Webhook call authentication and data minimization check
dast_recommendations.test_objective: Confirm the Notification Service webhook call is authenticated and does not transmit more customer data than necessary.
high_level_steps: Capture a live webhook call in an authorized test environment.
Verify presence and validity of request signing or mutual-TLS authentication.
Review the payload fields against the documented minimum necessary data.
dast_recommendations.expected_secure_behavior: The webhook call is authenticated and transmits only the minimum necessary customer data.
dast_recommendations.safety_note: Use test/sandbox third-party endpoints where available; avoid sending real customer data during testing.

action_items.title: Implement server-side object-level authorization in Account API
action_items.description: Ensure every Account API operation validates that the caller owns or is delegated access to the requested account/customer resource.
action_items.validation: DAST-001 passes and code review confirms centralized, server-side authorization enforcement.

action_items.title: Retire or re-secure the legacy mobile-to-database sync path
action_items.description: Route the offline sync path through the API Gateway and Account API with equivalent authentication, authorization, and encryption, or remove it.
action_items.validation: DAST-002 passes and network review confirms the Account Database no longer accepts unauthenticated direct connections.

action_items.title: Authenticate and minimize data in the Notification Service webhook call
action_items.description: Add signed-request or mutual-TLS authentication to the webhook call and reduce transmitted fields to the minimum necessary.
action_items.validation: DAST-003 confirms authenticated calls and minimized payload.
